osmo_revision_3.superseded: where a job exists in several versions, the report uses the latest (highest suffix); earlier versions ran with settings corrected later (three-anchor packing law, 0.5 ms, 1000 iterations, narrower bounds). rod-sand-cal3 exhausted its 6 h budget during the sensitivity analysis and was rerun as rod-sand-cal4 with a 16 h budget, its batches spread over four GPUs. rod-sand-cal4 searched in the rotated combination coordinates of the sensitivity analysis, where 16 of 30 search trials decoded outside the bounds (rejected_training); rod-sand-cal5 searches the parameter box itself with up to 8 generations

plate_intrusion.scale: 8.5 % of the largest measured lift of each medium (0.03 N/cm^3 for poppy seeds LP)

notes: Run times were measured while other runs shared the GPU.
The plate-intrusion training set and bounds were chosen after the literature sweep and the rejected 2 ms calibration.
Clay tests 1 and 3 used the first clay batch, tests 6 and 8 the second; laboratory SHANSEP parameters come from the first batch.

The other four media used the training points of poppy seeds LP and bounds and scales from rules fixed before their runs: friction sin(phi - 9.3 deg) to sin(phi + 4.5 deg), scale 8.5 % of the largest measured lift.
Li et al. measured the plate friction 0.40 for aluminium on poppy seeds only; the glass literature runs assume the same value.

Revision 3 runs use at most 1000 rheology iterations, except the plate sinkage of experiment E (250; 1000 changes it by less than 1 %); revisions 1 and 2 used 250 (Section 3.1 quantifies the difference).

revisions.summary: first version: loosely packed poppy seeds, centrifuge clay at 0.5 ms, rake workflow
four further media of Li et al. (2013), held-out plate-intrusion results at 0.5 ms, clay results at 0.25 ms, cloud rerun of the published poppy-seed sweep; earlier numbers unchanged

revision 3: rod intrusion at controlled packing (Ruck et al. 2025), rod pull-out (Douglas et al. 2026), probe penetration in dry loam (Mishra et al. 2018), plate sinkage in moist field sand (Kruger et al. 2023; Kruger 2025); study of numerical uncertainty; restructured text with Appendix A
